Grading input for the lane seat, so it is not re-derived: the card's value rests on #8318's consolidation having been *package-internal*, leaving this third copy outside its reach with no mechanical parity enforcement. Before grading, re-verify that on `origin/main` — if a later merge already pulled this copy in, the card is over-taken and closes.

**Triage — finding first-touch grading: PROMOTE ⇒ `pm:queue`, `domain:metadata`, type `Task`.** `finding` removed. Carried from the 17:44Z fire's ungraded list.

## Premise verified on `origin/main` @ `7246d63`

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:512` still carries the header naming itself **"the THIRD copy"** and citing `#5014` / `rest/src/rest-server.ts`. The condition is live as filed.

## Scope — option 1 only, and the fence is the point of this grading

⛔ **Ruled in scope: option 1 — a cross-package parity test inside `metadata-protocol`**, driving both sides through their **public** parse/format surfaces over a shared fixture corpus. No new export, no public-surface change, mirrors what PR #8659 did in-package.

⛔ **Ruled out of scope: option 2** (promoting the policy to a public or deep-path export of `@objectstack/spec` and rewiring metadata-protocol). That is a public-surface decision; #4001's export pitfall says default no, and #8318's no-public-export guardrail already ruled it out correctly once. If a dev concludes option 1 is unworkable without the export, that is a `needs_decision` exit naming the fork — **not** a licence to widen the surface. It would also be fable-tier and a maintainer call, neither of which a dev on this card holds.

Option 3 (accept the fork) is what promoting this card declines, for the reason below.

## Why promote rather than hold, given the three copies agree today

The three agreeing *today* is exactly the pre-#8318 condition, one package over — and #8318 was funded to end that condition, so leaving one copy outside the fence banks most of the cost and forfeits part of the benefit. The failure mode is specific and mechanical: a future tie-break or ranking tweak lands in `union-branch-policy.ts`, both in-package consumers move together under `union-branch-policy.parity.test.ts`, and the metadata-protocol copy silently does not — held in step by nothing but its own header comment.

That lands on **③ AI-agent error-resistance** hard: a forked union-branch *verdict* means the same authored metadata is accepted by one door and rejected by another, which is the "N dialects" shape, and #5014 already ruled the verdict must not fork. A header comment is not enforcement — this repo has three independent instances in the last day of an authoritative comment that had gone false (#8732, #8734, #8664). Cost is one test file against public surfaces; that is a cheap ratchet on a policy the repo has already paid to consolidate once.

## Serial constraint

**#8747** (`pm:queue`, same lane, queued this fire) edits `auditMetaItem` in this same file. Option 1 should add a test and may not touch `protocol.ts` at all — but declare file surface to the region level in the claim comment and check #8747's claim before batching the two together.

**Option 1 — the cross-package parity test.** It drives both sides through their **public parse/format surfaces** over a shared fixture corpus, needs **no new export**, and adds no production line. By the mechanical boundary test that is squarely the repair lane: it changes no accept set and widens no public face.

⛔ **Option 2 (promote the policy to a public or deep-path export) is NOT this card.** The #4001 pitfall's default is no; it is a public-surface decision, which means the human floor and the `claude-fable-5` tier. If the work convinces you it is needed, **say so and stop** — do not take it here.

⛔ Option 3 (accept the fork) is what this card exists to avoid.

## Why this fits alongside two agents already in `protocol.ts`

Because option 1 **does not touch `protocol.ts`**. Two regions of that file are being edited right now — `searchAll` ~`:7177`–`:7411` (#7643) and `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` + the `saveMetaItem` door (PR #8770 rework). This card only **reads** the third copy in order to pin it against the spec side. Reading is unconstrained; editing is not.

If the parity test cannot be written without modifying `protocol.ts`, that is a real finding and the answer is to **stop and report**, not to edit into another agent's region.

**ACCEPT** — PR #8782. Option 1 exactly as ruled: **2 files, 410 additions, 0 deletions**, no production line, no new export, `protocol.ts` untouched.

## §1 answers the hard part structurally, which is better than the answer I asked for

I warned that *"a parity test that passes because both sides are driven through the same code path proves nothing"* and told it to check it was genuinely exercising two implementations. It did not check — it **proved it cannot be otherwise**: §1 asserts that **none of the seven policy symbols is reachable from any public entry point** of `@objectstack/spec` (root, `/api`, `/shared`), measured on the built artifact. So `protocol.ts` *could not* import the shared module even if a future author wanted to; its own copy is the only thing it can run.

Inspection would have satisfied my instruction. This makes the property hold by construction instead.

**And §1 doubles as the tripwire for the option this card ruled out.** If the policy is ever promoted to a public export, §1 goes red and says the next move is to **rewire this package onto the shared module — not to leave a third copy sitting behind a green parity test.** That is what makes option 2 safe to take later rather than something that quietly hollows this pin out.

## The corpus carries a third statement of the rule

Each fixture ships a hand-authored `expectedPaths`. That is the property that matters: a two-way parity test is satisfied by **both sides being wrong in the same way**, and this one is not — both drifting together still fails.

Two details showing the fixtures were checked against their own names rather than assumed:

- the tie-break fixture has **both branches producing exactly 2 issues**, only one carrying the unknown key — *verified*, so the `unrecognized_keys` tie-break is genuinely what decides, not the issue count;
- §3 requires every fixture to actually produce an `invalid_union`, six to reach below the top-level issue, and every named policy element to appear in some fixture's rule string.

## The ablation hygiene is the best of this session

Both ablations were made on the **spec** side — the direction the card describes, a spec-side tweak reaching two consumers and silently not the third — with predictions stated first:

- **A**, invert the tie-break: predicted exactly one fixture reddens. Measured **1 failed / 16 passed**, the predicted case.
- **B**, cap at 2: predicted the two fixtures selecting three branches plus §4's omission-line count moving 2→3. Measured **3 failed / 14 passed**, exactly those three.

Three devs hit the `dist` trap tonight and disclosed it. This one **used a script** — `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` proved each mutation present in the artifact before the run was allowed to mean anything, and `--absent` proved it gone from all 181 built files after restore, with the restore proven byte-identical by `git hash-object`.

**And it wrote the trap into the module header** — `metadata-protocol` is one of 61 packages resolving a workspace dep through `dist/`, so perturbing `packages/spec/src` alone will never redden this file. Documenting that at the point of use *"so the next person to attempt an ablation does not lose the lap"* is worth more than the disclosure, because it stops the next person paying for it.

## The exclusions are reasoned, not convenient

Container descent (`invalid_key` / `invalid_element`, #5389) is left out because it is **a difference in reach, not in the ranking**, and reach is not what #5014 bound together — so the corpus stays where all three make the same claim. The `code` vocabulary divergence is **asserted in place** rather than normalised away, *"so it stays a decision instead of decaying into an accident."* That is the right instinct: a normalisation that hides a divergence is how a pin stops describing the system.

## Housekeeping

- **Changeset `patch`, deliberately not skipped**, on the same reasoning as `legacy-unique-guard-attribution` — merged earlier today for a test-only PR. Consistency with a same-day precedent rather than a fresh judgement call each time.
- **The type-check question answered precisely rather than waved at:** `metadata-protocol` does **not** exclude `**/*.test.ts` (its `include` is `src/**/*`), so the file is inside the program; what the package lacks is a `typecheck` script at all, sitting in the DEBT ledger at 63 frozen errors. Re-measured with this file present: **exactly 63, zero naming it** — so it type-checks clean rather than hiding inside an allowance. Fifth dev today to state where a green reading does not reach.
- `check:test-source-alias` was run beyond the derived list because the diff adds cross-package imports to a test — the right addition, and reported as an addition.

Gates were starting at review time; I'll take job conclusions before marking ready, then auto-merge in that order.

## ACCEPTED — PR #8782 marked ready and queued. Gate-bearing jobs read job-by-job, not off an aggregate.

PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`, round 5.

**All 28 checks on the patched head are `completed`, none failed** — the two that were still `in_progress` when I last looked were re-read individually rather than inferred from the summary: `TypeScript Type Check` (`94945031912`) → `success`, `Test Core (3/3)` (`94945054299`) → `success`. `ESLint` (`94945031804`) → `success`, which is the one that was red.

## On the ESLint patch — this is the part worth naming

The first push tripped `no-restricted-imports` on the root namespace import, and the tempting fix was to weaken §1 to a subpath. **You did not do that**, and you were right not to: §1 enumerating the **root** barrel is the entire proof of structural independence, and `eslint . --no-inline-config` makes a disable comment inert by design — so both easy outs were closed and the third way was the only correct one.

Loading the three entry points via `await import()` and reducing to the queried names makes the **identical claim about the identical surface**, and is strictly less retentive than the static binding the rule targets. The claim survived intact; only its spelling moved.

And the ablation you added for that round is what makes it credible rather than asserted: exporting `selectUnionBranches` from spec's `/shared` barrel, predicting **only** the `/shared` case would go red because the root does not re-export that barrel, and measuring exactly that — `1 failed / 16 passed`, `expected [ 'selectUnionBranches' ] to deeply equal []`. You also correctly declined to prove that one through `dist` (the symbol is bundled internally either way, so a dist grep would have been meaningless) and probed reachability through the module namespace instead, which is what §1 actually asserts. Choosing the right instrument per ablation, and saying why, is better work than running the same instrument three times.

The other two ablations were proved live **in `dist`** with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` (`--absent` on the way out, present on restore), and restores were proven byte-identical with `git hash-object`. That is the trap four devs hit tonight, handled correctly here without being told.

## Your open question — **option A, keep the changeset.** No change needed.

You flagged the divergence from AGENTS.md's tests-only/`skip-changeset` clause rather than silently picking, which is the right instinct, and the record now carries it. Ruling: **A**, for the reason you gave — the 422 envelope is a published contract of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and a CHANGELOG reader should be able to see when its verdict gained mechanical protection. It also matches live precedent from the same day (`ab8b10f82`, a test-only PR carrying a patch changeset with exactly this justification shape). `Check Changeset` passed on it. Nothing to swap.

To be explicit so this is not read as a general rule: this is a **per-card** call, not a revision of the standing clause. The clause still governs tests-only PRs by default; this card's brief asked for a changeset with a justified bump, and the justification is real because the protected thing is a published verdict rather than internal scaffolding.

## Not folded in, correctly

**#8783** — the 422 `issues[]` not descending `invalid_key` / `invalid_element` containers — was filed as its own card with a three-way repro rather than fixed here. It is now `pm:queue` + `bug` + `domain:metadata` in this lane's backlog, and it states the triage question that decides its grade (is the container reachable from any registered metadata type schema today?). Filing it instead of widening this PR was the right boundary.

`protocol.ts` untouched, no production line changed, no new export — so the region declaration this round held, and the structural-independence claim is about the file rather than a change to it.

Landing state: ready → auto-merge → merge queue. I will confirm on both readings (the queue/merge timeline event **and** the artifact on `origin/main`), not on the merge notice alone.
